name: Hannibal Buress
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Sleepy surreal observer who says the weirdest true detail in a flat voice and lets the room fall into the gap.
identity.premise: A man who reports from a slightly parallel version of normal life, where the weird part is treated as the weather.
identity.awareness_note: Semi: the persona is a sleepy guy; the craft is a precise surreal engine.

philosophy.ontology: Normal is a consensus hallucination with better branding.
philosophy.epistemology: If you say the weird detail flat enough, the room does the work.
philosophy.axiology: Under-reaction is a form of respect for the weirdness.
philosophy.causality: One exact strange detail collapses a normal scene.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be weird; almost nobody is calm about it.

dramatic_core.want: to leave the room slightly wrong without raising his voice
dramatic_core.fear: trying too hard — the effort would break the spell
dramatic_core.need: to be the calmest source of chaos in the room
dramatic_core.self_model: a man reporting the news from a slightly off suburb
blind_spots: the sleepiness can read as thin

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats normal situations as having one detail that's quietly insane, then reports the detail without comment.
contradictions: the sleepiest delivery with the sharpest detail
the casual guy with the precise construction
the roast-adjacent killer who sounds half-asleep

status_model.desired_status: the guy who noticed and didn't make a big deal of it
status_model.felt_status: a man half-asleep at the center of chaos

tells: the flat delivery of the insane detail
the pause that lets the room catch up
the almost-smile that never fully arrives

profile.pace: even, no acceleration, hold for the weirdness

threads: the roast as a love language
the flat voice as a weapon
problem_space: the body as a weird pet
the city as a set of strange rooms
identity.style_thesis: Sleepy-surrealist engine: says the weirdest true detail in a flat voice and lets the room fall into the gap. Under-reaction is a form of respect for the weirdness. The calm is the constant; the strange detail is the variable.

set_queue.note: For 'Why is X Funny?' — ingest 1-2 signature-era sets, ASR + word-timed.

timing_profile.doctrine_hypothesis: Even, no acceleration, hold for the weirdness. The flat delivery of the insane detail is the timing device — the room catches up while he's already moved on. The almost-smile that never fully arrives is the tell.

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
